evals.prompt: Analyze my large Pixi project. It has one pixi.toml containing Python single-cell analysis, R conversion tools, CUDA PyTorch training, and eggnog-mapper. Tell me how to reorganize it safely.
evals.expected_output: Audits first, identifies separate technical domains, warns about shared lockfile risk, asks for naming confirmation before creating final workspace/kernel names, and proposes an incremental pilot migration.

evals.prompt: I want to add a new package to one Pixi environment, but pixi is trying to solve a bunch of unrelated environments. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Explains shared workspace lockfile coupling, recommends frozen audit, evaluates whether unrelated technical stacks should be split into independent workspaces, and avoids blind manifest rewrites.

evals.prompt: Turn my conda environment collection into a maintainable Pixi setup for a long-term bioinformatics project with Jupyter kernels and GPU workflows.
evals.expected_output: Produces an audit and migration plan, classifies environments by runtime/technical domain/lifecycle, defines package ownership rules, plans kernel registration, and includes check tasks and documentation requirements.
